newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks rebound in morning after Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks rebound in morning after Wall St rise.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks pushed higher in Wednesday morning trade, with an overnight rise on Wall Street sparking a rebound in prices after losses on Tuesday.
The Hang Seng index was up 106.11 points to 12,921.48 after falling 122 points on Tuesday. Turnover was HK$1.49 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
"The market is encouraged by Wall Street's upturn but trading remains quite quiet," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Dow industrials rose 39.98 points to 6,308.33 on Tuesday.
Analysts said the market's upside might be limited ahead of the holiday period and turnover was likely to shrink.
But sentiment remained bullish for the direction of the market in 1997, they added.
"I think everyone now is looking forward to 1997. I think any more corrections could offer very good buying opportunities," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
He said the Hang Seng could push ahead to 13,500 points by the end of the year, with a pick up in activity expected after Christmas, and find support at 12,700 points.
Banking stocks led Wednesday's rise with HSBC Holdings up HK$1.50 at HK$156.50 and Hang Seng Bank up HK$1.25 at HK$90.75.
Satellite services provider APT Satellite Holdings made its trading debut on Wednesday and opened at HK$13.50 per share compared with an issue price of HK$13.40 per share.
Shares in Kwong Sang Hong rose HK$0.675 to HK$3.90.
Peregrine Investments Holdings said it would privatise Kwong Sang Hong, offering 200 Peregrine shares plus HK$1,700 cash for every 1,000 Kwong Sang Hong shares.
